description: This document specifies the AES hardware IP functionality. Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) is the primary symmetric encryption and decryption mechanism used in OpenTitan protocols. The AES unit is a cryptographic accelerator that accepts requests from the processor to encrypt or decrypt 16 byte blocks of data. It is attached to the chip interconnect bus as a peripheral module and conforms to the Comportable guideline for peripheral functionality.

rows.Description: This recoverable alert is triggered upon detecting an update error in the shadowed Control Register. The content of the Control Register is not modified (See Control Register). The AES unit can be recovered from such a condition by restarting the AES operation, i.e., by re-writing the Control Register. This should be monitored by the system.

This fatal alert is triggered upon detecting a fatal fault inside the AES unit. Examples for such faults include i) storage errors in the shadowed Control Register, ii) any internal FSM entering an invalid state, iii) any sparsely encoded signal taking on an invalid value, iv) errors in the internal round counter, v) escalations triggered by the life cycle controller, and vi) fatal integrity failures on the TL-UL bus. The AES unit cannot recover from such an error and needs to be reset.
The global escalation input signal from life cycle is multibit encoded.
Critical fields in main control register one-hot encoded.
Auxiliary control register can be locked until reset.
Critical fields in GCM control register one-hot encoded.
The key can be loaded from a key manager via sideload interface without exposing it to software.
Key registers are not readable by software.
Data input and internal state registers are not readable by software.
Key registers are cleared with pseudo-random data.
IV registers are cleared with pseudo-random data.
Data input/output and internal state registers are cleared with pseudo-random data.
Internal state register cleared with pseudo-random data at the end of the last round. This uses the same mechanism as KEY.SEC_WIPE and is active independent of KEY.MASKING.

1st-order domain-oriented masking of the cipher core including data path and key expand. 1st-order masking of the GHASH operation. Can optionally be disabled via compile-time Verilog parameter for instantiations that don't need SCA hardening.
The main control FSM uses a sparse state encoding.
The main control FSM uses multiple, independent logic rails.
The cipher core FSM uses a sparse state encoding.
The cipher core FSM uses multiple, independent logic rails.
The AES round counter inside the cipher core FSM is protected with multiple, independent logic rails.
The CTR mode FSM uses a sparse state encoding.
The CTR mode FSM uses multiple, independent logic rails.
The GHASH FSM uses a sparse state encoding.
Critical control signals such as handshake and MUX control signals use sparse encodings.
The main control FSM moves to a terminal error state upon global escalation.

The main control FSM moves to a terminal error state upon local escalation. Can be triggered by MAIN.FSM.SPARSE, MAIN.FSM.REDUN, CTRL.SPARSE, as well as CIPHER.FSM.LOCAL_ESC, CTR.FSM.LOCAL_ESC, GHASH.FSM.LOCAL_ESC.
The cipher core FSM moves to a terminal error state upon local escalation. Can be triggered by CIPHER.FSM.SPARSE, CIPHER.FSM.REDUN, CIPHER.CTR.REDUN, CTRL.SPARSE as well as MAIN.FSM.LOCAL_ESC.
The CTR mode FSM moves to a terminal error state upon local escalation. Can be triggered by CTR.FSM.SPARSE, CTR.FSM.REDUN, and CTRL.SPARSE.
The GHASH FSM moves to a terminal error state upon local escalation. Can be triggered by GHASH.FSM.SPARSE, CTRL.SPARSE, as well as MAIN.FSM.LOCAL_ESC.
Upon local escalation, the module doesn't output intermediate state.

rows.Name: PER_1
rows.Description: 3'b001: Reseed the masking PRNG once per block. Invalid input values, i.e., values with multiple bits set and value 3'b000 are mapped to PER_1 (3'b001). This results in a max entropy consumption rate of ~343 Mbit/s.

rows.Name: PER_64
rows.Description: 3'b010: Reseed the masking PRNG approximately once per every 64 blocks. This results in a max entropy consumption rate of ~5.4 Mbit/s.

rows.Name: PER_8K
rows.Description: 3'b100: Reseed the masking PRNG approximately once per every 8192 blocks. This results in a max entropy consumption rate of ~0.042 Mbit/s.

rows.Name: AES_192
rows.Description: 3'b010: 192-bit key length. In case support for 192-bit keys has been disabled at compile time, setting this value results in configuring AES_256 (3'b100).

rows.Name: AES_256
rows.Description: 3'b100: 256-bit key length. Invalid input values, i.e., values with multiple bits set, value 3'b000, and value 3'b010 in case 192-bit keys are not supported (because disabled at compile time) are mapped to AES_256.

rows.Name: AES_GCM
rows.Description: 6'b10_0000: Galois/Counter Mode (GCM). In case support for GCM has been disabled at compile time, setting this value results in configuring AES_NONE (6'b11_1111).

rows.Name: AES_NONE
rows.Description: 6'b11_1111: Invalid input values, i.e., value with multiple bits set, value 6'b00_0000, and value 6'b10_0000 in case GCM is not supported (because disabled at compile time) are mapped to AES_NONE.

rows.Name: AES_ENC
rows.Description: 2'b01: Encryption. Invalid input values, i.e., 2'b00 and 2'b11, are mapped to AES_ENC.

rows.Name: CTRL_AUX_REGWEN
rows.Description: Auxiliary Control Register configuration enable bit. If this is cleared to 0, the Auxiliary Control Register cannot be written anymore.

rows.Name: GCM_INIT
rows.Description: 6'b00_0001: Initialization phase. Software configures the Initial Key and IV Registers. The hardware then performs two encryption operations to 1) generate the hash subkey and 2) encrypt the IV. Both results are loaded into the internal GHASH block. Once the AES unit is idle again, software can advance to the next phase. Possible next phases are GCM_RESTORE, GCM_AAD, GCM_TEXT, and GCM_TAG. Invalid input values, i.e., values with multiple bits set, value 6'b00_0000, and all other values in case GCM is not supported (because disabled at compile time) are mapped to GCM_INIT.

rows.Name: GCM_RESTORE
rows.Description: 6'b00_0010: Optional context restore phase. Software configures the IV and Input Data Registers to restore a previously saved AES-GCM context (IV and GHASH state). Possible next phases are GCM_INIT, GCM_AAD and GCM_TEXT.

rows.Name: GCM_AAD
rows.Description: 6'b00_0100: Optional additional authenticated data phase (AAD). Software inputs the AAD via Input Data Registers block by block via Input Data Registers. Possible next phases are GCM_INIT, GCM_TEXT, GCM_SAVE and GCM_TAG.

rows.Name: GCM_TEXT
rows.Description: 6'b00_1000: Optional plaintext/ciphertext phase. Software inputs the plaintext/ciphertext block by block via Input Data Registers, and retrieves the output ciphertext/plaintext block by block via Output Data Registers. Possible next phases are GCM_INIT, GCM_SAVE and GCM_TAG.

rows.Name: GCM_SAVE
rows.Description: 6'b01_0000: Optional context save phase. The hardware stops accepting inputs. Software reads the current GHASH state and IV via Output Data and IV Registers, respectively. The only possible next phase is GCM_INIT.

rows.Name: GCM_TAG
rows.Description: 6'b10_0000: Tag phase. Software inputs a single data block containing the length of the AAD and the ciphertext via Input Data Registers. The hardware then produces the final integrity tag. Once the AES unit is idle again, software reads the final integrity tag via Data Out Registers. The only possible next phase is GCM_INIT.
